dataset_title: Bench-scale long-duration membrane pilot for wastewater biogas upgrading: abstract-level observations
geography: Municipal wastewater treatment plant; exact location not stated in accessible abstract
material_scope: Wastewater-treatment biogas containing methane, carbon dioxide, and organic impurities upgraded in a bench-scale hollow-fiber membrane pilot
data_handling: Only discrete values and ranges stated in the publisher abstract are transcribed. Units and ranges are preserved; no recovery, energy, standard-flow conversion, curve reconstruction, or missing time-series data are inferred.
license_and_access: Publisher search metadata marks the paper as open archive under a Creative Commons license, but the exact license subtype was not verified from the accessible record. No article text or figures are redistributed in this extract.
transferability: Technical comparator only. The feed is wastewater-treatment biogas with organic impurities and the source-specific hollow-fiber module polymer is not identified in the accessible abstract. It is not roadside-grass biogas or a GreenHub upgrader design point.
limitations: No methane recovery, total upgrading energy, methane slip fraction, module area, membrane material, uptime fraction, or uncertainty is reported in the accessible abstract.
Feed-flow reference conditions are not detailed; the printed ft3/h values are retained without conversion to Nm3/h.
Long-run product composition ranges are not paired with individual pressures, stage cuts, and feed-flow observations.
The authors report that organic impurities could condense and dissolve hollow fibers; this is a qualitative pretreatment warning, not a quantified lifetime factor.
No GreenHub parameter, runtime default, process result, TEA, LCA, or Pareto calculation consumes these values.
